utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which continues to apply. Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, just before we commence, I have had an opportunity with Ms. Sandra D'Angelo and the registry to try and work out a system that is not so long-winded in reading out all the numbers. I hope that this meets with the Court approval. What we did on Friday was we provided to the registry an index of all the annexes in relation to the tabs, and Your Honours should have them in your bundle in any event. What I am hoping to do is to call out the tab that we will be referring to, and then the four last numbers, which would relate to that tab itself and indicate whether it's English or B/C/S, without repeating the previous 12 numbers. On the basis that, quite simply, that it is the -- it's targeted on the tab itself and the page numbers, and one should be able to find that. I don't know if that will speed things along a little and make it less complicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything that will achieve those objectives will be encouraged. We will try it and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Witness, we had reached -- it was tab 21, but in actual fact we were going through your notes. You had the translation, which had been typed up with your agreement and checking, and could you return to that page where it is actually down at the bottom right-hand corner, 6 of 17 and ET number 7792. Now, have you got the draft copy?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And have you got bottom right-hand corner, 6 of 17?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6 of 17, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You have that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And we were dealing with the reference to 0468-7770, which was the number of your original Kypr book. And just reading so we take it into context "we can make it possible to." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, do you wish to refer to the original document, would that make it easier for yourself, or would you prefer to refer to the typed copy?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can use the typed copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, indeed. Well, that being the case, it was originally in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was originally in B/C/S. And it started at 1615 and we were told that Serbs Territorial Defence volunteers will not allow convoy pass through if there is a single Croatian soldier in it. If the people knew that Ustashas were in the convoy, then would liquidate you, means European monitoring commission and us, JNA guard in the convoy. There is no agreement which could resolve that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. You have told us this, but let's just continue then.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As for us, we can follow through on that item, so we cannot guarantee to you or any wounded people to leave Vukovar if there is only one there."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we turn over to the original page ending in 7770. It was originally in B/C/S. And the translation which you agreed, what did that say then, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It follows the previous text: "We can make it possible too so believe that it will end tragically."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I assume that we will be stopped on our way and they will check it. We can't guarantee security but not in the case if they find somebody."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now when you were told this, did you ask any questions about who the people who were causing the trouble, allegedly, who they were?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it was longer discussion about that. We said that JNA is -- is superior power on this territory, and that General Raseta made this agreement and that JNA is responsible for the convoy. And we were told that the terrain is very difficult and that they can stop the convoy any -- anyway. According the remarks, you can see from -- from my books that there was during the discussion mentioned even Seselj volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there is a remark that: "They from/illegible/reason, will kill us all."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Now here was a situation, are they saying it is only the Seselj volunteers, or is it the case that it is wider than that and Seselj volunteers are part of that group?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was wider than that. Those volunteers were mentioned only as a part of that. Because you can see that Territorial Defence volunteers, so it covers more than only Seselj troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Here again is a situation where there is reference to that if any, I use the word, Ustasha soldiers are in your convoy, they couldn't guarantee your safety. Was there any plan to remove people who were preserved as being Territorials and dealing with them separately?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan, not according the agreement, not according our preparations for convoy. We were told that only this, that if there is anybody in -- in the convoy from mentioned groups, that we will be killed. So it's not -- it was not precisely mentioned what will be the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, what is the next entry that you have in your notes, please, from that briefing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We, JNA, are protecting those people, otherwise they would be killed immediately even though they are wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, let's just look at that for a moment. "We, the JNA, are protecting those people." Who are "those people," the people who would otherwise be killed immediately?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this sense, it is connected with those people of -- who are in the hospital as -- as Croatian soldiers. I understand -- as I understand the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what was your understanding then that what was to happen with the Croatian soldiers who were in the hospital? What was to happen to them?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I can only assume from this text that there was an intention of JNA to remove them and to keep them safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And is there any record at all in relation to that, any discussion in your records about that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, we were complaining that wounded prisoners of war are a part of this Raseta's agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Zagreb, and Colonel Cunningham really strictly rejected that many times, and I remember that Dr. Schou as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Rejected what?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To remove people from -- from the convoy or from hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What was the basis for their rejection or objecting to that proposed course by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a so-called -- I am using the term Raseta's agreement, so if I may to refer to some text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If you go, I think we have had already as an exhibit, but I think it's also at divider 20.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the text. It is the text. It's from the 19th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So what -- what was your understanding about the agreement that was going to happen to all those wounded and sick?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's paragraph 5 in this -- in this agreement: "The evacuation will include all those wounded or sick undergoing medical treatment in Vukovar Hospital who are judged by the authorities of the hospital to be fit to make the journey." There is no other possibility. Only authorities of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's just continue, if I may, please. I want to deal with your original page number 0468-7771, which was originally in B/C/S, translated into English.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we deal with that entry, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "They came to protest and we explained to them who would be permitted to leave Vukovar. There are some wounded officers who will be exchanged for ours."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, please, with "they," the word "they." "They came to protest and we explained to them who would be permitted to leave Vukokar." And, now, firstly who is this speaking? Is it ECMM?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And to what does this refer?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who -- what is the reason of that. I assume that it is -- it is when JNA was in a contact of Croatian forces in Vukovar, because there were -- I know that there were some negotiations going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the phrase: "We explained to them who would be leaving -- who would be permitted to leave Vukovar." Now, what do you mean by that, or what was meant by that, "who would be permitted to leave Vukovar"? Because under the agreement it seems to suggest that all wounded would be permitted to leave Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was -- I don't know what was the -- the explanation of the army to those people. I can't say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You can't remember?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Let's move then, please, to the next entry, which is 1635?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. 1635 there was presented a message from Zagreb ICRC, International Committee of the Red Cross, and the sentence I -- I wrote is: "Part of the wounded people have been taken out from the hospital without care."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, when you say "without care," in actual fact, I don't know whether on the typed version it says "problems." If it is, I think you looked at the translation and amended that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will do that, just a moment, sir. In original it says "bez brige," means without -- without care, without -- I understand that without appropriate medical care.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. If you would just --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the entry at 1635, here it's clearly somebody is speaking. Part of the wounded persons have been taken out of the hospital without appropriate medical care. Who is saying that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message came probably through International Red Cross, because the representative was there, but it could be done even -- even through ECMM sources. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, dealing with this particular entry, was that occurring 1635, the original briefing, the time of the briefing was 1615. Here we are at 1635, approximately 20 minutes later. Are you able to say that when you wrote this down who said it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether that was communicated to the JNA, that there was concern?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Because there is another sentence afterwards and it's the answer probably of JNA to -- to this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what was the reply, as far as you understand it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We don't know anything about it. I think that it is from Croat top to show that JNA is doing massacres against wounded people."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So as far as you are aware, that particular entry at 1635 --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- was communicated to someone in the JNA and that was the reply?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we just turn over the typed copy, please? Now, there is a question posed: "Is the JNA securing the hospital, and is there a chance that somebody is taken out without the JNA knowing about it?" Who posed that question, which seems to be a -- a natural flow from the earlier question and answer?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I can't say who is the author of that. I believe that it was somebody from ECMM delegation, or Dr. Schou or Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Schou or Cunningham. Now, there is a reference, a query about, well, is the hospital being secured or not and is there a chance that somebody could be taken out without the JNA knowing about it. What was the reply, if there was any reply to that? Did you make a record of that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have -- I have another record there, the second sentence afterwards the remark, and it is about three JNA soldiers, who are captured there were taken out from the hospital and they are in the Negoslavci hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But I think it's right it say that there is an entry just immediately before that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It -- it's the answer of JNA: "We cannot assume that before they took their wounded men from whom they thought."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, so the question is: Is the JNA securing the hospital and is there a chance that somebody is taken out without the JNA knowing about it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The answer is again, I think you had a problem with the translation?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will check the translation, if it is right. Just a moment. It's -- it's a wrong translation, because there are -- the answer is on -- I will repeat the question for -- for better understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Is JNA securing the hospital, is there a chance that somebody is taken out without JNA knowing it?" And the answer is: "No. We can presume or assume that before they took their -- those their wounded men for whom they have an interest or they sought."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And "they" clearly, presumably, relates to the Croats; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So try to clarify exactly what the reply was. It then goes on: "Three JNA soldiers who were captured were taken from the hospital and they are in the Negoslavci hospital."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What was the conclusion that the JNA representative made?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is not in -- in connection with -- with the sentence I have read or interpreted before. It's -- it's -- it's an information only that three JNA soldiers who were captured were taken out of the hospital and they are in the Negoslavci hospital, which means in JNA hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Let's deal with that point, if I may then, please. We've got reference by way of information, three JNA soldiers were captured, they were taken from the hospital, and they are in the Negoslavci hospital. Was there any suggestion that those JNA soldiers had been mistreated in the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that the Serb -- people of Serb origin were mistreated in Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And with regard to the three JNA soldiers, is there any reference to that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you just clarify why it is that there is no reference by you about allegations of Serb mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but it was said many times and it was a part of presentation. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we then move, then, please, to -- that finishes the 19th, that document. If we can just set that aside. I want to deal with number 20 -- tab 21. Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: As we have already established, this was a document created by Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And Cunningham was actually present with you when this briefing was given; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So let's just go through, as it is in slightly more detail. We've got the date, we've got the various individuals, and we have one name that I just want to deal with initially. You've got Colonel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now -- and he's down as what, please? What was the role assigned to him?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As JNA commander, Operation Group South in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: How was it that Colonel Pavkovic was supposed to be JNA commander Operation Group South, Vukovar, when he clearly wasn't?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You can see the -- this -- this part is written by -- not by Cunningham's hand. It is written by somebody else. But we wrote down the name of -- of JNA army representatives on the other side only in the manner we were -- we were told that they are. We haven't checked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You didn't check?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Very well. Let's then deal, please, with number 1 entry.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And for instance, there are even some mistakes in transcription because Major Saric is there mentioned, and it was Major Zaric. So there can be even some misinterpretation of names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. So you don't know how these names actually -- where they came from?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The JNA names. Well, let's deal, then, please, with halfway down the place we've got place, headquarter JNA in Negoslavci. You've got that there?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Point 1A, pertinent points follow. The whole city, including hospital, under JNA control.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now do you agree with that analysis or not, from what you saw?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's what we were told, that the whole city, including hospital, under JNA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So that was what you were told about -- by the JNA. "Hospital management replaced by" --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "By military doctors and personnel."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then there is reference to prepared -- "JNA prepared totally for their part of the evacuation." Now, I just want to turn over, please, to the next page, which is 1399. C refers to the route, but I want to refer to d, and paragraph 5. Now, if you can keep your finger on that particular page, but go to tab 20, which is the agreement that we have already referred to this morning -- well, this afternoon, and the Court already have it as an exhibit. This is the evacuation agreement. And let's just read this particular document. Is this the fax that you had received?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Right. Well, let's just read what 5 says: "The evacuation will include all those wounded or sick undergoing medical treatment in Vukovar Hospital who are judged by the authorities of the hospital to be fit to make the journey." Now, here we have -- well, have you any difficult with that? I see --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's turn to this page that is handwritten, the Cunningham document.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cunningham document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 of the fax.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Signed by Croat and JNA authorities. Evoked much discussion. Colonel Pavkovic stated that prisoners of war would not be allowed to depart. As far as the prisoners are under JNA control, second, if he did, Serbs irregular/local citizens would attack the convoy. Three, the prisoners of war would be exchanged for JNA prisoners of war at some future times."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, here you have the faxed document, what I'm going to call the evacuation agreement, if I may, and here you have, quite simply, this entry in the Cunningham document stating that "evoked much discussion." Well, here was a situation being stated to you that the prisoners of wars are under the JNA control. Well, what was actually then going to happen, because it was -- it was contrary, was it not, to what the evacuation agreement said?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- it was -- it was contrary to the agreement, so it's why Colonel Cunningham argued with -- with -- with JNA authorities, please follow the agreement. It's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when you say Cunningham argued, how forcefully did Cunningham argue?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a very strong military man, but -- but not shouting. He was -- he was only stressing the importance of the thing, because it was one of those crucial parts of agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what sort of things was he saying about the apparent breach of the evacuation agreement?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, did he agree or did he disagree?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he disagree. He disagreed that it is not possible not to obey the signature of General Raseta who swear in the name of JNA that it will be fulfilled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did the Geneva Convention or any of those particulars feature in the discussion?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, could you be kind enough to tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, would you like to try to remember generally? Basically what I want to know is what the ECMM position was in relation to the breach of the agreement vis-a-vis various obligations.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a simple statement that there is violate the Geneva Convention. It's -- we have to stress it each time when we saw that -- that there are some violations of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when you -- when --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I believe that it was mentioned even by International Red Cross representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, we'll due with that in due course, but I want to deal with you, please. You were present at the time and were present when Colonel Cunningham stressed in a forceful way about the breach of -- alleged breach of the evacuation agreement. So can you help the Court, please, what was said when Cunningham declared that he was not happy?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, really, on that. I know it was -- it was generally said, but concretely I -- I have no detailed --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's deal with the prisoners of war are under JNA control. What was going to happen to those prisoners of war? Did you inquire about that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after the evacuation of Vukovar's hospital or before?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It could be both. It's really for you to answer. The question --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I finish? The prisoners of war under JNA control, clearly you would have been interested in what was going to happen to them at some stage, or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the evacuation there was violate the agreement of -- signed by General Raseta. So we insisted that the agreement should be fulfilled and if there are some wounded prisoners of, some wounded people from Croatian army, that they should be evacuated to Croatian side, according article 5 of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I ask then the following in relation to number 2: If he did Serb irregulars/local citizens would attack the convoy. Was it ever suggested to extract from these prisoners of war people who were considered to be Croatian soldiers, defenders, whatever generic term you wish to use?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We strictly denied it, and we said that we will risk it and that we wished to have convoy as it is, so with all the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Let's move on to E, if I may.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Colonel Pavkovic" -- if it be Pavkovic -- "did not know the state of the hospital and did not know how it might be used in the future." How did that arise, please, that entry? And f, if you would wish to read f as well, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means that the situation in the hospital was really very difficult, and it was not clear if it can still be used as -- as -- for medical care. So if the patients in hospital who can't be moved, how to -- how it is possible to provide the necessary care for them --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's deal then with paragraph 2. It deals with the involvement of the International Committee of the Red Cross. May we deal with that, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Involvement with Red Cross was very limited, and I am not certain what arrangements they have made writing list of wounded persons to be moved or if then they have determined and agreed a" -- I don't know. "Of neutrality, as para 6 of fax."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Shall we look at paragraph 6 then, please? Divider 20, page number 1397.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Republic of Croatia and the Yugoslav People's Army will recognise the neutrality of Vukovar Hospital during a period covering the evacuation. The hospital will be put under the protection of the ICRC who will advise both parties of the period of neutrality which they require."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So can we just deal then with paragraph 6 vis-a-vis the ECMM position for monitoring. Here you've got in paragraph 6 the recognition or apparent recognition of the neutrality of the Vukovar Hospital. Can I help you, Ambassador? You seem to be looking for another document.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. So we -- during the discussion there on the meeting, we recognised that there is an intention of International Red Cross to go to Vukovar's hospital before -- as soon as possible in the afternoon or in the evening, and that they will make -- they will make a list of people who are there and they will prepare appropriate -- appropriate evacuation scheme for them and so on and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, rather than so on and so on, can we just look please at the phrase: "The hospital will be put under the protection of the ICRC."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What is meant by "under the protection of the ICRC," as you understand it at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That everybody will respect them as the highest authority on the -- on the spot, as concerning humanitarian and medical care.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And as far as you are aware, was that something that the JNA agreed at the meeting, what I will call the Colonel Pavkovic meeting?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, can you just look to see if there is any reference to disagreeing, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. And just for completeness sake, can we just see what the bottom entry is on page -- what I call the -- have you got it there, Ambassador?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Page 1399, it's the reference to para 6 of the fax message. It seems to be -- it says: "For RCB"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is here. For RCB. Thus will monitor move of refugees and hospital evacuation."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I -- sir, may I? There is another reference in another message --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- on that, so I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I just deal with this.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I just deal with this, and then I suspect I will be able to take you to another document. But may we just deal, please, with the "four RCB teams will monitor." What does that mean then, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means there will be four -- four groups of Red Cross people who will monitor the removal or evacuation of refugees and the hospital evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said that you wished to refer to another document. Which tab is that, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the tab 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 31. And it's the task we got from tasking cell we got from your headquarters, missions headquarters in Zagreb, on the 19th of October at --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there in article 5 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, can I just -- before we move on, I will give the numbers so that we all know what we're talking about, because I can move to that straight away. So this would be tab 31. It's actually 65 ter number 253, as far as I am aware. The English version is 1446, and the translations from the B/C/S 3619.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I mean another -- I mean 1443. It's the task for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, what we will do is, it's ERN 00381442 running through to 00381446. In reality, it's 1446 through to -- 1442 to 1446. If we just turn to that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And is it possible for that B/C/S version to be put on the screen for the Defence? It would be -- it really should read "message form." In actual fact, it's 1443 is the one that I'm looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: While that's just being clarified, Ambassador, could you just that the document that you are referring to, does that have at the heading "message form?"

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, message form. And I will check it, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And it should have as its first format, it says: "Fax message urgent." And it's five.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I think go back one more.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If you go back one more page on the original.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So if you go to your tab 31?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. So the first page indicates that it is a fax. It has five pages; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If we go to the original, you may find that more helpful than the actual -- would you go to the original, Ambassador, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subject is evacuation of Vukovar's hospital, the 20th of 11th. And the date of document is the 19th of November. We got it in 2214 minutes on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And we can see that from the top of the page and the fax -- fax number. Can we turn the page, then, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Page 1443. And this, again, is a message form coming through?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And it's to whom then, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message is to liaison office, Belgrade, and to teams Alpha and Charlie in Djakovo because there were already prepared teams from I think Zagreb who will follow the convoy during the way, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And am I right in saying that when you say "liaison office," that is actually different, because there appears to be comma between liaison office, or officer, and Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Belgrade, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So there are two different locations, not just one?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Belgrade means Belgrade centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And liaison office is where?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Very well. Let us then look at entry one, then, please. What does that say?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Entry one is: "Evacuation Vukovar's hospital, the 20th of November, 1991. Attached agreement of 18th of November refers meeting in Zagreb today. Decided the following: Number 2, loading of wounded will start the 20th, 8.00 in the morning."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So the 20th, I think it says November, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: 20th of November, 8.00 in the morning, is the loading of the wounded; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3: "Handover of wounded by JNA to Croatia authorities will take place in Zidine at the specified cross-roads, the 20th of November at 11.00," probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In the morning?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And 4, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4: "We are informed all wounded are transportable."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So all wounded are transportable?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. 5?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5: "The rules of Geneva Conventions will apply to all wounded prisoners of war, i.e., they will be interviewed individually and privately." Probably it's paragraph 5 convention, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 continued, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Continue, yeah, continue. "To ascertain where they want to go."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. And 6?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6: "ICRC will compile a list of all wounded being evacuated from the hospital and check that they are all loaded on the transport. They will then check the wounded on arrival at Zidine according to the lists to ensure that they have all arrived at the handover point. Red Cross have undertaken to have sufficient personnel to" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Perform"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Perform," yes. "Perform this" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Function"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Function." And the point 7 is: Monitors from liaison office, Belgrade, will monitor the operation from the hospital in paragraph 7 continues, Vukovar to the handover point in Zidine to ensure that the agreed procedure have been complied with by all" -- I can't read it. It's illegible for me. "Parties" maybe. And there is another by another handwritten to the fax that: "The Red Cross will travel from Vukovar with the convoy to carry out this function." Point 8: "Teams from Zagreb and Belgrade to make" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It's either "easy" or "early" but I --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Early communications, checks and ensure That they keep lock" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Each other informed"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Each other informed on" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Progress"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Progress," maybe, yes. Yes, it's progress. "As well as headquarters in Zagreb." 8A: "Remind both sides of obligation to cease-fire."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And point 9: "Regards to all."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, we've got the drafter's name in the bottom right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's the head of the tasking cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Just when we'll dealing with it, just for completeness sake, I'm going to ask the Court to refer to tab 29 which, I hope, will reveal another document. Which is -- if I may get my notes. It's ERN 00381437 going up to 1438 with a B/C/S translation of 03040263 to 264. The document that I would seek to adduce, and might I just make application in any event to make an exhibit of tab 31 documents, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be exhibit number 315.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then can we deal with the -- the document that I have referred to, we will come to it again in due course in tab 29, but the fourth, top right-hand corner, 4 of 4, it's page number 1436. I hope that it will be a typed copy, which gives -- should be coming to the command of the 5th Military District. Is that on the screen in B/C/S or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I will --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the end of -- of the -- the previous message from --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm just going to -- Ambassador, I'm just going to try to deal with this and then come back. Because I'm trying to deal with five documents at one time. So how is that translation -- I've got the English version. Has the translation arrived or the defendants' screens yet? It's 1436, the last four numbers of tab 29.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have it, but it is not in B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I've got it now, in B/C/S, I hope. On my screen. Do the defendants have it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, but it is not the same text as 1436, as you mentioned. 1436, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can do 145. I don't see how it can be myself. Is that it now? It should read to the command of the 5th Military District.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have this original, but it is not -- just a moment. Maybe it is inside the text somewhere. No, it is -- it is not the text. It is not the text. Maybe I can put the -- the B/C/S version to the display.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, but we have got an extremely expensive e-court system that should be able to almost sing and dance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am in the Court's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I believe they are trying to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: There, we've got it now.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we deal then with the English version?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The English version is an original.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. We've got to the command of the 5th Military District, care of General Raseta.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Raseta. Zagreb, November the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, do carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Accordingly to the oral agreement reached on November 20th about transfer of wounded and ill from the Vukovar's hospital and the refugees convoy from Vukovar, we are informing you that the Croatian side has agreed with your suggestion to receive about -- above-mentioned convoys from the army in the village of Bosanska Raca."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then I think it goes on to refer to that they would be ready for the reception?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It lists wounded inhabitants of Vukovar, and then without going into any great detail, the final paragraph, if I paraphrase it, we're asking for a written guarantee from the JNA for safe and undisturbed movement. And then finally: "Oral agreement for the passage on above-mentioned relation, we have reached during talks with the president of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the November the 20th at 2245." And then there is a reference to the number of wounded and sick, and refugees. Now, clearly it's a little later in time, but, as far as you are concerned, was there any difficulty about the route itself at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have only indirect information as a member of EC monitoring mission because I was not in the -- as monitoring those -- those other ways of convoys, so I took part only in two convoys from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there were much more convoys, I believe, five or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Well, there is no other question that I was to ask you about in relation to tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could I ask, please, for the tab 21 documents to be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit number 316, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'd like to now move on, if I may, to tab 22, and also -- and perhaps more particularly initially, the translation of your -- what I call the Kypr notebook and you've got the copy of it. Again, it should be again, if we look at that document, the typed version, it should be bottom right-hand corner, 7 of 17?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we just put our hand on the typed version and also open our file at tab 22? Because tab 22 says: "Humanitarian convoys from Vukovar's hospital, November the 20th and 21st, special report by Mr. Kypr, November the 22nd, 1991." Now, can I just, by way of clarity, before I proceed to produce it in evidence, are you able to say if this is your handwriting or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told there may be difficulties showing both documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, shall I deal with it this way: I'll deal with one document at a time. I'll just clarify the -- what I will call tab 22 to confirm, although I think the witness has confirmed it is his document written by him. I will then moved on to the typed version of the original notes, work from that, and then return to the other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The issue is whether the accused have paper versions or are they dependent on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: They would be reliant upon the screen. But there is the B/C/S translation of the typed version, and there is also a B/C/S translations of tab 22. So we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That means they have to be brought up in the Croatian -- B/C/S version and not the document you are working on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Oh, I -- I understand that perfectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, the document that I am going to be working from, the defendants have got a hard copy of it. As far as I am aware. We provided hard copies to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's true for the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But not the tabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: On the tabs we have to do that by e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So what I will do -- well, I'll leave that to the end and I'll deal with the hard copy English version/B/C/S version, which I hope will be relatively clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, then, please with your notebook commencing on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Where did you stay the night on the 19th; can you remember?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And we have seen timings, clearly, that I think the evacuation was to occur in the early morning of the 20th?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you remember at what time you returned to Vukovar, approximately?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately before -- before -- before 8.00. Or roughly 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, then, please, with your first entry that you have?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly Vukovar means -- means Negoslavci, because it was the point near Vukovar where we got the -- the first information briefing, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So we have got Negoslavci, N-e-g, I presume?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Do feel free to consult your handwritten note, if you're concerned.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So Negoslavci, does it is mean Negoslavci or does it mean Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Negoslavci was a village near Vukovar which was used as a point for negotiation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. But I would like to know is were you in Vukovar per se, or outside of Vukovar or Negoslavci? Because, Negoslavci, I think, is about 10 kilometres away from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So in this early morning briefing in -- in the 20th we were in Negoslavci, according my -- my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And did you attend a briefing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And as far as you are aware, who was giving that briefing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is written that it was Colonel Pavkovic, but I don't remember a real person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And what were you told in the briefing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told that there are houses near hospital, that they are mined, maybe even some wounded people have explosives, that some streets are still mined.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that the whole organisation is "our" - means JNA jurisdiction - and that gentlemen from ECMM can just monitor but object later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you explain to me what you mean "just monitor and object later"? What exactly does that mean or did it mean to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Observe situation and if we are not satisfied with something or if something is not according the -- the agreement, we have to -- or we are able to -- to complain or object only later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Only later. So if you saw something occurring at the time that did not meet with your approval, what were you obliged to do? Complain at the time or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did you make any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. What else was said then, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The wounded men of paramilitary formations should stay here. That is definitely a solution with General Raseta."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You referred to "our" -- "our jurisdiction." What did the "our jurisdiction," "the organisation is our jurisdiction." Who is the "our"? ECMM or JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, JNA. Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What is the next entry then, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next entry speaks about problems which ECMM has to cover. First it is convoy of refugees, and there is a -- let's say sketch how the convoy should be -- should be built from cars, so it means that first will be military police, then car of ECMM, then cars of convoy and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- so on. And the other problem of ECMM is the evacuation of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You've referred to that second part, the evacuation of the hospital, but I just want to move two lines prior to that. The phrase: "The wounded men of paramilitary formations should stay here. That is definitely a solution with General Raseta." Now, "paramilitary formations," who did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that time I remember that this name was used in -- in a various context. Very various context. Sometimes even -- even Croatian National Guard and MUP were -- were addressed or were named as paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, but we have seen from the evacuation agreement that it related to all wounded.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: That's correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And here we have: "The wounded men of paramilitary formations should stay here." So you have one hand the Raseta agreement saying all wounded would be evacuated, and here you've got the JNA, Colonel Pavkovic, if it be him, saying that the wounded men of the paramilitary formations should stay here. Now, did that raise any topic of discussion?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see on the other page, the next page, there is a response of Colonel Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Before we get there, what about the entry: "That is definitely a solution with General Raseta." Who said that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A representative of JNA. I don't know who, whom it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I just see if I clarify this: What is being said is that the wounded men of the paramilitary formations would stay here and that's definitely a solution with General Raseta. Now, if we turn the page, can we deal with that entry, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Who does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Colonel Cunningham --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- relating to Raseta in Zagreb. He objected that all wounded should be transported, that rules of Geneva Convention will be applied on all prisoners of wars, of all prisoners, and that International Red Cross will provide it a list of all wounded evacuated from hospital and check them in transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we just deal then please with that situation. Here we have the Raseta agreement, I have already mentioned it three or four times, you have got the JNA briefing saying, quite simply, that Raseta has said, apparently, that the wounded should remain, and Cunningham saying the rules of the Geneva Convention will be applied on all prisoners of war. Now, when he said that, was there any reply by the JNA? Did they agree or disagree or not comment at all?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. During those discussion, even on the 19th, we repeated this message many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, did it seem to have any effect?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regard to the "will be applied on all prisoner of wars," not just injured people, all prisoner of wars, there is a distinction, is there not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a distinction because Cunningham speaks about Geneva Convention, not about Raseta's agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. But let -- can I just ask you, please, on all prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It's not a case of all wounded; it's a case of all prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Do you understand the distinction, Ambassador?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, what was said in relation to all prisoners of war? Was there any agreement to that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's a standard procedure. Geneva Convention is the part of the highest law at all, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. But forgive me, here you have a situation where the JNA are saying wounded people will be retained, if they're believed to be --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- Croatian defenders. And here would you have Cunningham, your boss, saying that all wounded should be transported, rules of the Geneva Convention will be applied on all prisoners of war. Now, some might say that this is a situation of conflict or disagreement. Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we then deal, please, with the ICRC, reference to that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the next remarks --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that ICRC should -- will check wounded by list on the beginning and after the transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Sorry, it's my fault. You did refer to this. ICRC will provide lists of all wounded --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- evacuated from the hospital and check them in transport. Was there any representative of the ICRC present at this briefing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And as far as you are aware, was there any disagreement by him to that proposed course, that the ICRC would basically be responsible for the -- for the loading?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he was objecting that -- that he was not allowed to go to the hospital in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you remember if there was any explanation by the JNA why he was not allowed to go in the evening?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's deal, then, please, with the next page, 0468-7774 in the original English.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "International Red Cross will check wounded by a list on the beginning and after the transport. International Red Cross has enough people for it."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So with regard to the ICRC and that briefing in the morning, what was your understanding? That the ICRC were going to be responsible for the control of the evacuation or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They will -- they will be responsible for the control of hospital if they can get it. And that they will follow the convoy with -- with wounded people and that they will provide the evidence of those wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Again, if there had been any objection by the JNA to the ICRC taking control or indicating that they would control the evacuation, if there had have been an objection, do you think you would have recorded that in your notes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there was a discussion between, but it was afterwards between representative of JNA and -- and ICRC near the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to the bridge in due course. Let us move on, please, to 8.30. Well, perhaps, actually before I move to 8.30. So when that briefing concluded, the briefing in the early morning and the one we have just been discussing, what was your understanding, what was the role of the ECMM to be?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role of ECMM was -- was done by the -- the task which I have mentioned in the tab 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You mean observe and object later?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. The ICRC, what was its function?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: ICRC should take control on the hospital, keep the -- or taking care about the neutrality of the hospital, provide the list of wounded people, check them and make those humanitarian tasks, which are they are using -- which they are used to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us deal then, as I say, with 8.30 in the morning. It's the -- it's the same entry.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: To what does this relate, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "JNA got the message from the zone commander from the zone for exchange of refugees."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So, I beg your pardon, could you repeat that again, please. "JNA got the message from the zone commander from the zone for exchange of refugees."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's my explanation of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could you read the text out and then provide an explanation.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "8.30, colonel spoke with the zone commander for exchange."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Which commander was that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Was it a JNA colonel or was it Colonel Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was JNA colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And he spoke with the zone commander for the exchange. Which zone commander are we referring to?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Do we know which zone?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was zone Nustar-Marinci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And how did you obtain this information?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told it on the briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, that's 8.30.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: 8.30 in the morning you were still in the briefing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the next entry, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "When it comes to JNA road Nustar-Marinci is completely safe."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "He has no contact with the opposite side, he did not notice any demining from" -- plus means cross-road or crossing point "in direction of Nustar."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: When you're referring to "he," are you referring to a JNA colonel?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the spot, from the zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Can we then deal with the next entry at 7775? To which does that relate, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It's only the pair of names, which I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, are they in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but I think that it's really -- there are no -- I can show it that it has no -- any connection or any referring to other parts. It is an extra page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. But can I just ask you: Is it in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, just a moment, sir. The first one, yes, and the second one, yes, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And one seems to say: "Deputy, 1st Military District"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So where did you get that information from?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From somebody from JNA. We are told it was all the time that we were told he and he is that and that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what about the next name?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Colonel Ivezic, head of hospital."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And, again, were you informed of that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we turn over then to 7776.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now it seems to be a name, Bozo Dzapic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bozo Dzapic, born 1967.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it is written the name and the date of delivery was in my hand, and the rest is written in Latin by Dr. Schou. It's a diagnosis of one of wounded or ill men who had to be left in the hospital in Sremska Mitrovica because he was -- he was not able to move further to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And I think then there was one other entry relating to Koritnik is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Koritnik. Doctor of medicine, Zeljko Koritnik. It is written probably by somebody else. It's not my hand. And it was, I believe, one of the doctors from Sremska Mitrovica hospital where the convoy was overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's then move on to the documents, because that concludes your what I call original notes prior to and/or at the same time as the evacuation. But if we go to tab 22, that has to now be shown to the defendants, please in B/C/S. And I'm told it's 03033931 to 3935. Could I be told, please, when it's shown? Is it now showing? Thank you very much. Ambassador, would you be kind enough to turn to this agreement which you have agreed is in your hand. It was compiled on the 22nd and relates to the 20th and 21st of November?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's just deal firstly with the time schedule, as you recollect it. ?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The 20th, arrive Negoslavci at 6.45 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6.45 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Due to depart to Vukovar 8.45?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, yes, certainly. Waiting at Vukovar's centre --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until approximately 10.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then the loading patients and others until approximately 1430. And then arrival at Negoslavci at 1300.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is it 15? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then departure to Sremska Mitrovica at 1530 and arrival at 1700 hours. Can we just deal then with the 20th? Here you've got contact names. Now, the handwriting, as I say, I think is yours. When you have written down Colonel Pavkovic, how have you come to the conclusion that it was Colonel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I was told that there is Colonel Pavkovic, and I wrote down this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the position as you thought it was, you've already got him as commander?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it means deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Operation Group South.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And you've assigned each person a number?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Again, these -- these names, can you just read them out, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Number 2 is Lieutenant-Colonel Ivezic, deputy of number 1 for communications. General -- number 3 is General Jerko Crvenic, Deputy Commander of 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So the same position as Colonel Pavkovic, that seems to be. Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljko Koritnik on duty in medicine centre in Sremska Mitrovica. Number 5, Bozo Dzapic, wounded, sent to Belgrade. Number 6, Nicholas Borsinger, representative of ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, again, we've already done your notes. So when we have this briefing by one, as you refer to it, is it right, if I take it in short order, that in actual fact this briefing is the same, or has the original Kypr notebook has been used to compile this particular document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, but not only this one, I use the one even remarks of -- of Mr. Cunningham and others' knowledge, because there were more monitors. And it is written on the 22nd when we came back to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I deal with A, briefing by 1. And I want to deal with the third point, please, starting "the wounded members." Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could you read that, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The wounded members of so-called Croatian paramilitary forces must stay here (we have been told later by patients that they have been captured and left the hospital before our arrival). As well as some people of former personnel - Dr. Bosanac."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now I just want to deal with that part of the entry, if I may, the brackets part, which clearly was not in the briefing because it was subsequent to your arrival?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "We have been told later by patients that they have been captured and left the hospital before our arrival." Now, from your timetable you arrived, or you certainly were waiting in the centre until 10.45. What time do you think you actually got to the Vukovar Hospital at?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10 minutes later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. So it would appear that -- you that were told this. Now: "They had been captured and left the hospital before our arrival." That's the wounded members of the Croatian paramilitary forces. Even though you have been told that you are not to make any comments, observations until after it was all over, that was the brief that you were given by the JNA, did you at any time approach any member of the JNA and say, Just a moment, we understand from patients that a number of wounded soldiers were -- use the phrase captured and removed before either ourselves or the ICRC arrived?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. There were -- there were first we asked for the Dr. Bosanac, because she was in Serb press or Serb media represented like Dr. Mengele. So we -- it was our main fear that she can be in a threat. And so we asked where she is, and then we were informed by patients and by some people there, I don't know whom, that she was captured. And then we were told officially that she will be -- she will be put before a court. According those prisoners of war or wounded -- wounded people, we asked through our liaison officer, it was Colonel Cunningham who asked that, that we wish to know what had happened with them and how they are treated and so on, and we got no question -- no answer on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let us just deal with -- well, actually just before I move on. When Cunningham asked this question, can you remember when Cunningham asked it? What is it at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it -- it was somewhere in the hospital because he -- not having the -- the answer, he has to work on that so he went after certain time being in hospital for half an hour, one hour, I don't know for how long because I was very busy, he went for Belgrade to -- to resolve the situation, to work on our other convoys and -- and he got an information with -- with him that there are missing persons [realtime transcript read in error "concerns"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, we've reached the time when we must break for the tapes to be changed. Is that a convenient --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, could I just clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I mean this in no discourteous way, because the learned -- the Ambassador speaks so many languages. But at page 43/5, the phrase that was used "to resolve the situation, to work on our other convoys, and he got an information with him," can I just clarify, when you use the phrase, "He got an information with him there are missing" -- I thought he said "persons" not "concerns," got an information, do you mean that he had been informed?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On the -- on the -- on the translation, I've got "there are missing concerns." Is it concerns or persons?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
