utterances.text: Yes, this is the copy of the report, copy of the paper we got the next day after referendum when we went to Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The report which bears the number 00381387 in B/C/S or 03037649 in the English translation is actually the result of the vote in the referendum on the decision of the citizens of Ilok, if they wanted to surrender their weapons or not; is this correct? It states in line 1: "Report on the referendum held on the 13th of October, 1991, on deciding on the surrender of the whole or entire quantity of weapons."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And the agreement with the JNA. And the result, evident from the report, is that out of 3.553 citizens who participated in the referendum, 940 voted in favour of surrendering weapons and signing the agreement with the JNA, while 2.619 voted against.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the counsel says 519.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: That was one of my questions. Could you please now look at report numbered 00381388? English translation is 03037650. Is this a report on the referendum vote to decide on the second referendum question and that was the decision to move out of the town altogether because of the crisis situation?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, which document do you refer to, which tab do you mean?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's tab 12, and it's the next document right after the one that we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What I would like to know is whether this is the report on the vote on the second referendum question to decide whether to move out of the town or not because of the crisis situation?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The results here are out of 3.553 citizens altogether, 2.577 voted in favour, and 5.437 decided against.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 797 voted against.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I would like to have the documents in tab 12 with the numbers indicated be tendered into evidence. I think we could give the documents one number, because these are two referendum questions, but it's only one referendum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received and given a number now, Mr. Vasic. But under the normal procedure you would include that in your Defence folder so that it can be accessed. It's normally undesirable for the registry to access the Prosecution folder to borrow a document for you and make it an exhibit. So if could you arrange for that to be dealt with overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. The Defence is in the position that perhaps our learned friend would tender that, because it was in the Prosecution's folder. So we were surprised that they did not do it. But of course we are going to do it that way, so we will resolve that this evening and we will have an exhibit that will be marked as a D exhibit. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 324.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kypr, would you be kind enough to turn to tab 18? That's a document with the number 00381383, in English, to 00381384, and the B/C/S translation has the number 03040699 and 03040790. This is a report of the monitoring mission regional centre in Belgrade drafted on the 18th of October; is that correct? 1991.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure, because there is the date there written hand is the 18th of October, but the date in the -- in the row, RCB patrol assignment is the 19th. Probably, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be kind enough to read what it states in item 1 of the report? It has three subparagraphs.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Contact with Colonel Grahovac at 1100 hours on Ilok's bridge from Colonel Grahovac. A, Ilok and villages Sarengrad, Bapska, Mohovo, Lovas are safe and quiet and under JNA control. JNA find 15 tonnes of explosives in Ilok. Residents of the village will have no problem if they want to come back."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that this was the actual situation on the 18th and 19th of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. What I know is that when the evacuation of Ilok started I had to move for Belgrade for another task, so I believe that I was not there in this area. So I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham was in this area at the time and he was part of the monitoring mission, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not. If you can see page 1383, the team consists of Finakaliotis, Bonnemann, Deprez, and somebody else who is cancelled I don't know if he was there or not, but there is no name Cunningham. Cunningham is there in special instructions mentioned. And it is probably asked them, it means Kypr and Cunningham, for briefing, but I don't remember that. No, for briefing, it is -- it is writing to those -- next sentences, I believe. I can't explain that. But Cunningham was not a member of the team. At least it is not written here in the names and nationalities. He was there during the evacuation, but not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did the team have instructions to meet with you and Mr. Cunningham on the 18th of October?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it is in a special instruction, as I have mentioned. There is a remark: "See Kypr/Cunningham 18th October for briefing." It's only --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is after each -- each mission there is a debriefing, or if some other teams are going then there is a briefing for them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, we have reached the hour when we must adjourn. And we resume tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
